The capped metric power matrix 3^t(J-I)+(1-3^t)A1+(2^t-3^t)A2 is conditionally negative iff every displayed lambda_j(t)<=0. At t=0 each is -1 and the isometric J(8,4) submetric bounds the common admissible exponent by log(2)/log(3); Schoenberg fractional-power inheritance makes this a single initial interval. In n>=4k, the quadratic eigenvalue envelope has its peak at j=k-1, giving the stated unique zero and centered Hilbert rank defect. Its fixed-k and rank-density limits use small-t Taylor expansions and selection of theta_j/k near its maximizing shell. Independently checked numerical spectral first zeros for 84 (n,k) pairs with k=4..15 and n=2k through 9k, confirming all relevant bounds and unique k-1 mode when n>=4k. These finite checks do not replace the proof at arbitrary parameters.
